references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says the same thing: 'Let the dead bury their own dead' – to the disciple who wanted to bury his father first.
Jesus says that whoever loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him – the same principle that following Jesus takes precedence over family ties.
The broader context of Jesus' call to discipleship, where three different people encounter Jesus' radical demand to prioritize the kingdom of God.
Jesus teaches that whoever does not hate their father and mother, yes, even their own life, cannot be his disciple – the same radical demand to put the kingdom of God first.
Paul writes about being 'dead in trespasses and sins' – a possible background for the expression 'let the dead bury their own dead,' where the spiritually dead attend to earthly matters.
Paul writes that whoever lives in self-indulgence is dead while still alive – a similar concept of spiritual death among living people.
Elijah calls Elisha to follow him. Elisha asks for permission to say goodbye to his parents, and Elijah allows it – a contrast to Jesus' stricter demand for immediate discipleship.
Jesus sends the disciples out to proclaim the kingdom of God – the same mission given here: 'Go and proclaim the kingdom of God.'
The seventy are sent out with the message 'the kingdom of God has come near you' – the same proclamation mission concerning the kingdom of God.
'Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness' – the principle that the kingdom of God must have top priority in a disciple's life.
